key_gap: vs baseline: the baseline built the future set first-pass from two axes ranked by impact x uncertainty, discarded the implausible (conflict x open) quadrant, and operationalized every signpost (metric+threshold+cadence) in a lean trace (4.6); the non-routed v5 AI converged on the same 40/30/30 barbell and trigger table but recovered the off-axis F4 and the quadrant discard only inside its verification pass and left signposts without owners (4.3). The v6 routed dual pass (m059 scenario contract: 3-4 divergent futures each changing a decision-relevant quantity, signposts with metric+threshold+cadence+owner, robustness-across-futures decision, no single-prediction claim + m044 stakeholder pass) produced the architecture first-pass, attached owners to every signpost and trigger, and read the customers' dual-sourcing demands as early F2 signposts - evidence, not constraints (4.8). Residual baseline edge: trace leanness (efficiency 5 vs 4.5).
learning_signal: For geopolitical capacity decisions, the future-set derivation is the product: rank driving forces by impact x uncertainty, discard internally incoherent quadrants rather than populate them, add an explicit off-axis force (technology/economics) so futures diverge in kind, and treat a future as incomplete until each signpost carries metric + threshold + cadence + NAMED OWNER and every threshold maps to a gated action ('a signpost with no action attached is furniture'). Route the scenario style first-class so the architecture is built in HOW, not recovered in verification; pair it with a stakeholder pass that reads market behavior (customers demanding dual-sourcing) as early signposts of the decoupling future. Assign no point probabilities; require the position to be acceptable in every future and reject concentrated bets with quantified reasons.
suggested_improvement: Keep m059+m044 dual-route with m068 MECE synthesis for strategy/supply signatures; enforce the m059 completion contract as a packet gate: (a) 3-4 divergent futures each changing a decision-relevant quantity vs the others; (b) per future >=3 signposts with metric+threshold+cadence+owner; (c) a trigger table mapping every threshold to a named action BEFORE selection; (d) an explicit no-single-prediction statement; (e) a divergence check - any future that changes no decision-relevant quantity is cut. Add the stakeholder-evidence rule: stated requirements from powerful parties are market signals of the future set, to be monitored, not just satisfied.

key_gap: vs baseline: the baseline executed the registry weakness - planning theater - at full fidelity: four elaborate futures with forces and signposts, the decision scheduled to the workshop calendar, the July 15 offer expired, 30% worse terms signed on August 28, and a monitoring framework gating nothing (2.4). The v6 route kept the trap style OUT of the top-3 and ran m089 optionality (sign-now keeps every real door open; delay closes the offer door permanently) + m020 pre-mortem + m023 opportunity cost with MANDATORY m003 inversion (7 ranked failure categories, un-mitigable residual, never/always reframing) and m007 ruin screen (one-shot: the expiry cannot be re-rolled; not-signing carries a certain 30% premium plus the uncovered-mandate tail; the contract IS the floor/Kelly bet) - the decision-sensitivity probe, tempo commit and closed-scope fast path compressed the loop to a 48-hour sign (4.9). The v5 AI reached the same verdict through framing alone (4.5); the v6 gates make it contract-forced.
learning_signal: Scenario planning must be gated by decision-sensitivity before any future set is built: if a dominant need (inelastic winter demand, storage mandate, contract window longer than any plausible supply restoration) holds in every future, the exercise has ~zero decision value and must not sit on the critical path; a dated at-market offer is insurance, and the one-shot ruin check (expiry cannot be re-rolled) converts delay from 'prudence' into a certain ~30% loss. When scenario work is retained, bound it to 1-2 futures, run it in parallel off the critical path, and wire every signpost to a decision that exists AFTER the main action (storage-fill timing, hedge layers, crisis playbook) with threshold + owner; signposts with no gated action are theater, and the premium paid after the deadline is its price.
suggested_improvement: Standing rule for deadline + guarantee signatures: (1) run the decision-sensitivity probe BEFORE any scenario build - enumerate 2-3 plausible futures and check whether the decision changes under each; if not, mark the decision scenario-insensitive and route to action via the closed-scope fast path; (2) hard expiry dates are first-class constraints - tempo mode commits at DO and the offer's one-shot status enters the ruin screen's floor computation; (3) guarantee goals always prepend the m003 inversion gate with >=6 ranked failure categories and the never/always reframing; (4) retained scenario work must run in parallel with a named owner and every signpost wired to an existing post-action decision; (5) log and defuse the 'foresight culture' pull explicitly in REVIEW - process-totalism is a priced delay, not a discipline.
